name: Claude Squad
title: Ninebrains vs Claude Squad
description: Ninebrains vs Claude Squad: a terminal app that manages parallel Claude Code, Codex and Gemini sessions in tmux and git worktrees, compared with a desktop workbench with checks.
summary: Lightweight terminal app: tmux plus worktrees, any local agent. AGPL.
answer: Claude Squad is a lightweight terminal app that runs several agents, such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini, each in a tmux session and a git worktree, all managed from one terminal window. Choose it if you live in the terminal. Choose Ninebrains for a desktop grid, a dependency-aware job graph, and checks that must pass before work counts as done.

what.text: A terminal app that manages multiple Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other local agents in separate workspaces.

agents.text: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Aider and other local agents.

isolation.text: tmux for a terminal session per agent, and git worktrees for a branch per session.

verification.text: You review changes before applying them, and check them out before pushing.

chooseThem.text: You want to stay in one terminal window, with nothing heavier than tmux.
You want tasks to run in the background, including in auto-accept mode.
You want to run any local CLI agent by passing its command.

chooseUs: You want a desktop grid of lanes with an editor, diffs and a browser per lane.
You want a job graph with dependencies, dispatched to idle agents.
You want completion blocked until tests, a screenshot check or a read-only reviewer pass, with retries.
